criteria.statement: An initial scaffold into a project with no `.gitattributes` creates `<project>/.gitattributes` containing the line `.claude/verification-notes.md merge=union`
`scaffold-project.sh --refresh` on a project whose `.gitattributes` is absent, or present without the union line, leaves the file containing `.claude/verification-notes.md merge=union`
When the project already has a `.gitattributes` with other lines, scaffold and `--refresh` add the union line without changing, removing or reordering any existing line
Running scaffold and then `--refresh` (and `--refresh` again) never duplicates the union line: it appears exactly once
A failure while ensuring `.gitattributes` (e.g. the path cannot be written) prints a warning and neither the scaffold nor the refresh aborts: it completes and exits 0
`isRecordFile(path)` returns true for `.claude/verification-notes.md`, for `.trd-state`, and for any path under `.trd-state/`, and false for `.trd-statex/...` and for ordinary source paths
`classifyClash(paths)` returns `{ recordOnly, notRecord }`, where `notRecord` lists exactly the input paths that are not record files and `recordOnly` says whether every path is a record file
`record-files.js merge-base-in --base <ref> --branch <name> --pr-head <sha>` prints exactly one JSON line and exits 0, for a success, a refusal and a stop alike
`mergeBase` refuses with `ok: false` and changes nothing when the current branch is not `<branch>`
`mergeBase` refuses with `ok: false` and changes nothing when `HEAD` does not contain `<prHead>`
`mergeBase` refuses with `ok: false` and changes nothing when a tracked file outside the record files has uncommitted changes, and does not refuse for uncommitted changes confined to record files
When merging the base in produces no unmerged paths, `mergeBase` commits the merge and returns `ok: true`, `outcome: "clean"`

When every clashing path is a record file, `mergeBase` rewrites each as the union of both sides, commits the merge, and returns `ok: true`, `outcome: "resolved"`; the committed files contain both sides' lines and no conflict markers
A record file that clashes with no common-ancestor version (both sides added it) is still resolved as the union of both sides
When a resolved `.json` record file does not parse, `mergeBase` aborts the merge and returns `ok: false`, `outcome: "stopped"`, naming that `.json` file; `HEAD` and the working tree are as they were

When any clashing path is not a record file, `mergeBase` aborts the merge and returns `ok: false`, `outcome: "stopped"` with `notRecord` listing those paths; `HEAD` and the working tree are as they were
A record path that one side modified and the other deleted is not unioned: `mergeBase` stops with `ok: false`, `outcome: "stopped"`, naming the path, and `HEAD` and the working tree are as they were
The local merge honours the project's own `.gitattributes`: with the union line present, opposing edits to `.claude/verification-notes.md` merge without a clash and both sides' lines are kept

Custody classifies record files by the shared rule: `.claude/verification-notes.md` and paths under `.trd-state/` classify as record files, `.trd-statex/...` does not, and the work's own TRD still classifies `ignored`; `custody.js` defines no record-file list of its own
The merge step's contract has a new step 1, before the custody gate, that reads `gh pr view <pr> --json mergeable,state` and skips the step when the state reads `MERGED`
While `mergeable` reads `UNKNOWN`, the merge step polls up to 8 times, 15s apart, and if it is still `UNKNOWN` goes on to the custody gate rather than stopping

On `CONFLICTING`, the merge step fetches the base and runs `record-files.js merge-base-in`; on `ok: true` it pushes the branch, polls until the PR's `headRefOid` equals the pushed commit, waits for CI on that head as `wait-ci` does, stops on a CI failure, and only then runs the custody gate and merges
On `ok: false` from `merge-base-in`, the merge step stops, naming the offending paths, and does not proceed to the gate or the merge

The merge step's "One rule for every stop" list includes the new stops, and the rule to commit and push nothing between the custody gate and `gh pr merge` is still stated, with the new push placed before the gate

End to end on a real GitHub PR whose only clashes with its base are record files, `/ship-build`'s merge step merges the base in, pushes, waits for CI on the new head, passes the custody gate and merges the PR instead of stopping
